digest:
The day’s papers weave a rich tapestry around holographic dynamics and the geometry of black holes, with several works sharpening the bridge between bulk geometry and boundary observables.  In particular, the exact mapping between the finite‑velocity drag force on a heavy quark and the tension of the entanglement membrane reveals how nonlinear momentum loss encodes the butterfly velocity and probes the near‑horizon geometry, while the universal high‑frequency exponential rate in holographic thermal two‑point functions is shown to be governed by a WKB spectral curve that captures the black‑hole singularity.  Complementing these bulk–boundary insights, the bootstrap‑driven study of four‑point correlators involving giant gravitons uncovers a hidden ten‑dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing the correlators to be expressed via SO(2,10) rotations and generating functions, and the BPS bootstrap analysis in Ô=4 SYM further delineates horizonless geometries from black holes through large‑N matrix bounds.  On the side of exact solutions, the first non‑extremal rotating AdS black holes with four independent STU charges are constructed, and their BPS limits reproduce microscopic entropies, while a new rotating instability in BFSS matrix theory points to a non‑axisymmetric branch in the gravity regime.

On the mathematical front, a quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlevé II is established via rank‑three Wakimoto–Whittaker modules, linking irregular KZ–BPZ equations to an irregular Gaudin oper in the Nekrasov–Shatashvili limit, and a categorical random‑matrix theory framework predicts exact degeneracies in 1+1‑dimensional CFTs by treating twisted Hilbert spaces as tube‑algebra representations.  The modular‑unfolding approach to type IIB instanton corrections extracts both continuous and cusp contributions to higher‑derivative terms, while the q‑oper construction in ADE algebras unifies Q‑functions and QQ‑relations with affine opers, resonating with the quantum Langlands picture.  Finally, several papers touch on scattering‑amplitude structures—multiloop unitarity from Airy zeros, massive‑vector recursion, and tripartite magic diagnostics—providing new tools that could be leveraged in celestial‑amplitude studies, even though no paper directly addresses celestial amplitudes today.

papers.title: Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra
papers.abstract: A tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state if and only if its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. These conditions are quantified using anti-flatness, giving a diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that is computable and experimentally measurable using randomized measurements. In non-abelian quantum doubles, it appears only when the triple points of the tripartition lie on plaquettes. In random tensor networks, it appears exactly when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that a tripartite pure state is locally equivalent to a stabilizer state precisely when its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra are flat, offering a computable and experimentally accessible diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic. It further shows that this magic emerges in non‑abelian quantum doubles when triple points of the tripartition sit on plaquettes and in random tensor networks when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects, providing a new probe of holographic entanglement structure.

papers.title: Four-charge Rotating AdS Black Holes in Gauged STU Supergravity
papers.abstract: We present an exact solutions for non-extremal rotating AdS black holes with four independent charges in four-dimensional gauged STU supergravity. The scalar potential introduced by gauging breaks the hidden symmetry underlying solution-generating methods in the ungauged theory, making the construction of such solutions a longstanding challenge. We analyse the global properties of the solution and derive its thermodynamic quantities. We further take the BPS limit and show that the resulting entropy agrees with the known microscopic result obtained from the dual conformal field theory.
papers.summary: The authors construct the first exact non‑extremal rotating AdS black hole solution carrying four independent charges in four‑dimensional gauged STU supergravity, overcoming the obstruction posed by the scalar potential. They analyze its global structure, compute thermodynamic quantities, and verify that the BPS limit reproduces the expected microscopic entropy from the dual CFT, confirming holographic consistency.

papers.title: More physics at the entangling surface: boundary conditions and entanglement in 2d TQFT
papers.authors: Jackson R. Fliss, Alan Rios Fukelman, Stathis Vitouladitis
papers.abstract: We present a systematic treatment of entanglement in two-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). Our approach clarifies the sensitivity of entanglement measures to the cutting maps that implement Hilbert space factorization. Such maps embed the TQFT Hilbert space into a description with potentially more degrees of freedom, and for entanglement to be well defined they must be isometric, i.e., they must preserve the norms of all states. We show that the na\"ive cutting map based solely upon path integration subject to boundary conditions is not isometric for generic TQFTs. For any 2d TQFT, we give a prescription to construct isometric cutting maps by dressing path integration with suitable edge operators. This allows us to compute entanglement for any state, any bipartition, and any boundary condition. As a consequence, we find a non-integer "ground-state degeneracy" \`a la Affleck-Ludwig, despite all boundary conditions being gapped. We further show how to reconstruct the partition function of the TQFT at arbitrary genus from the multi-interval R\'enyi entropies of a single state. For theories with (possibly non-invertible) symmetries, we show that the entanglement entropy of the symmetric ground state can distinguish gapped phases with the same symmetry, without any further knowledge of their vacua, while the entanglement asymmetry of the vacua entropically detects symmetry breaking. We illustrate our formalism with a range of applications, from finite gauge theories to Haagerup gapped phases and infrared phases of adjoint QCD$_2$.
papers.summary: This paper develops a systematic framework for defining entanglement in 2d topological quantum field theories by constructing isometric cutting maps that incorporate edge operators, enabling the computation of entanglement for arbitrary states and bipartitions. It also shows how multi‑interval Rényi entropies can reconstruct the full partition function and uses entanglement measures to distinguish gapped phases with identical symmetries.

papers.title: Type IIB instanton corrections from pure modular unfolding
papers.abstract: We study the reconstruction of instanton corrections to type IIB higher-derivative interactions from their low Fourier modes using modular symmetry, without invoking supersymmetry differential equations. This provides a framework for studying non-BPS interactions through their modular coefficient functions. For the $D^6R^4$ coefficient, Rankin-Selberg unfolding determines the continuous spectral overlap from the complete zero mode. Assuming the conjectured simplicity of the even cusp spectrum, we extract the cusp amplitudes from Mellin residues of the complete first mode. We combine both contributions to reconstruct all higher Fourier modes, using Hecke relations for the cusp contribution. Using the Kuznetsov trace formula and bounds on the spectral tail, we derive the $g_s^{-1/2}$ and constant terms in the weak-coupling instanton prefactor at every fixed positive charge. The leading term arises collectively from the infinite cusp sum, and both coefficients agree with the known expansion. With incomplete low-mode data, we construct modular ambiguities and give sufficient conditions for the stability of leading higher-charge coefficients. Applied to the supplied $D^8R^4$ data, these results identify the additional information needed for higher-charge predictions.
papers.summary: The paper develops a modular symmetry–based framework to reconstruct instanton corrections to higher‑derivative interactions in type IIB string theory, avoiding supersymmetry differential equations. By applying Rankin–Selberg unfolding, Mellin residues, and the Kuznetsov trace formula, it extracts both continuous and cusp contributions to the $D^6R^4$ coefficient and outlines a method for higher‑point corrections.

papers.title: Holographic Drag Force and the Entanglement Membrane: Geometric Reconstruction and Information Spreading
papers.abstract: A central question in holography is how different boundary observables encode and reconstruct the geometry of the gravitational dual. In this work, we uncover an exact geometric correspondence between two seemingly distinct aspects of strongly coupled dynamics: the dissipative drag force experienced by a moving heavy particle(quark) and the entanglement membrane governing the propagation of quantum information. We show that both constructions retain the same underlying structure of the geometry, leading to an invertible transformation between the finite-velocity drag force and the geometric membrane tension. This correspondence reveals that nonlinear momentum loss encodes detailed information about entanglement dynamics: the leading nonlinear correction determines the butterfly velocity, while higher-order terms successively probe the local geometry of the membrane near the horizon. We further connect this hierarchy to scalar pole-skipping, establishing an all-order relation between nonlinear dissipation and near-horizon spectral data. The shared geometric structure also has implications for quantum information recovery, with the quintic drag coefficient determining the leading dependence of information velocity on initial entanglement. Conversely, the complete information-velocity curve provides a reconstruction of the reduced bulk geometry along the physical interior membrane branch, complementing the exterior reconstruction from drag. We show that stochastic momentum broadening supplies the additional radial information needed to reconstruct the complete exterior metric up to an overall scale. Our results thus reveal how dissipation, entanglement dynamics, and spectral properties provide complementary access to holographic geometry, establishing a unified framework for understanding the geometric information encoded in distinct boundary observables.
papers.summary: The authors uncover an exact geometric mapping between the finite-velocity drag force on a heavy quark and the tension of the entanglement membrane, showing that nonlinear momentum loss encodes the butterfly velocity and higher-order corrections probe the near-horizon geometry. This correspondence also ties to scalar pole-skipping and enables reconstruction of the bulk geometry from boundary dissipation and entanglement dynamics.

papers.title: Moduli spaces in CFT: vortex defects
papers.abstract: We construct and study a class of codimension-two conformal defects in CFTs with spontaneously broken conformal symmetry, assuming that a continuous global symmetry is also broken on the moduli space. Our construction can be viewed as an analytic continuation of the saddle point describing large charge operators and generalizes known BPS defects in supersymmetric theories, such as Gukov-Witten surface operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM and vortex loops in ABJM theory, but does not rely on supersymmetry. These defects are characterized by continuous, unbounded parameters controlling the expectation values of operators parametrizing the moduli space, and interpolate between a quantum regime and a semiclassical regime in which the local physics approaches that of the symmetry-breaking vacuum. This connection allows us to derive exact results from the effective description of the broken phase. In particular, our results for Gukov-Witten surface operators agree with localization, and we compute the $g$-function for a broad class of $1/2$-BPS vortex loops in ABJM theory. Finally, we relate the spectrum of defect operators, in a suitable scaling limit, to the spectrum of massive particles in the symmetry-breaking vacuum.
papers.summary: The authors construct codimension‑two conformal defects in CFTs with spontaneously broken conformal symmetry, generalizing BPS surface operators such as Gukov‑Witten and vortex loops in ABJM. They use an effective field theory of the broken phase to compute exact defect observables—including the g‑function and defect operator spectra—matching known localization results and offering a bridge between quantum and semiclassical regimes.

papers.title: Categorical RMT
papers.authors: Chuanxin Cui, Kristan Jensen, Sridip Pal, Moshe Rozali
papers.abstract: Random matrix theory (RMT) describes the level statistics of chaotic systems one symmetry sector at a time. We propose its analogue for local quantum systems on a circle with ordinary or non-invertible symmetries. Symmetry defects define twisted Hilbert spaces, and the symmetry sectors are irreducible representations of the tube algebra, which acts within and between these spaces. Under our proposal, the symmetry fixes exact degeneracies and identifications among sectors, and ordinary RMT describes the rest, with unrelated blocks treated as statistically independent. We call this categorical RMT. For a non-invertible symmetry it goes beyond ordinary RMT, since Hilbert spaces with different twists can share a sector, and so part of their spectrum, though no invertible symmetry relates them.   We confirm this in a chaotic Fibonacci anyon chain, and check the framework in chaotic $S_3$ chains. We extend categorical RMT to primary states at fixed spin in 1+1-dimensional CFTs, where modular covariance requires additional correlations. For continuous symmetries, the Sugawara construction and spectral flow isolate a neutral spectrum, which can have symplectic statistics even in a bosonic theory. In holographic CFTs, torus wormholes decorated by the SymTFT or by Chern--Simons theory realize the predicted ramp and its modular completion.
papers.summary: The paper extends random matrix theory to systems with (possibly non‑invertible) symmetry defects by treating twisted Hilbert spaces as representations of the tube algebra, leading to a categorical RMT that predicts exact degeneracies and block‑wise independence of spectra. In 1+1‑dimensional CFTs and holographic settings it connects modular covariance, SymTFT‑decorated wormholes, and Chern–Simons dynamics to the spectral ramp, offering a new statistical framework for chaotic quantum systems.

papers.title: BPS Bootstrap
papers.abstract: We apply the large $N$ matrix bootstrap technique to constrain expectation values of simple operators in heavy BPS states that are dual to classical geometries. For states dual to horizonless geometries, their explicit moduli give rise to large allowable regions in the bootstrap, while for black holes, a converging bootstrap should find islands. We explore this method in $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ super Yang-Mills theory at large $N$, working at weak coupling and focusing on BPS states with scaling dimensions of order $N^2$. For the $1/2$, $1/4$, and $1/8$-BPS sectors, the bootstrap finds large regions, in agreement with an eigenvalue description of such states in the limit of large charges. We also present preliminary results for a BMN truncation of the $1/16$-BPS sector, which contains states dual to both horizonless geometries and black holes. Isolating the black hole states in the bootstrap remains a challenge.
papers.summary: The authors employ the large‑N matrix bootstrap to bound expectation values of BPS operators in $mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, distinguishing horizonless geometries from black holes via the size of allowed parameter regions. Their results confirm eigenvalue descriptions for 1/2, 1/4, 1/8‑BPS sectors and hint at a convergent bootstrap for 1/16‑BPS black hole states, though isolating them remains difficult.

papers.title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
papers.authors: Alessio Caddeo, Oscar Henriksson, Carlos Hoyos, Mikel Sanchez-Garitaonandia, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez
papers.abstract: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.
papers.summary: The paper develops an improved scalar‑fluid effective theory for thermal first‑order phase transitions, linking spinodal instabilities to the sign of the specific heat and validating the results with a holographic model. It also extracts a friction coefficient governing bubble wall velocity from a holographic correlator, refining the hydrodynamic description at long wavelengths.

papers.title: Resummations In Higher-Curvature Modifications Of Starobinsky Inflation
papers.abstract: We study higher-curvature corrections to Starobinsky inflation, which are expected to be generated at the quantum level. When treated perturbatively in the couplings $\gamma$ of the higher-dimensional operators, these terms produce inverse powers of the slow-roll parameter $\alpha$, casting doubt on the reliability of the slow-roll expansion. If instead $\gamma$ is kept exact, the expansion fails to reproduce the Starobinsky model smoothly as $\gamma\to 0$. We show that this problem is solved by resumming certain series in the ratio $\alpha/\gamma$. The resulting ``improved'' slow-roll expansion is regular in the limit $\gamma\to 0$ and gives the same result whether one expands first in $\gamma$ or in $\alpha$. We illustrate this explicitly for an $R^3$ term, obtain the power spectra, spectral indices and tensor-to-scalar ratio at next-to-leading order in the improved expansion, and show that results in the recent literature are recovered as the first-order Taylor expansion of ours. Comparing with the latest ACT, Planck and SPT data, we find that the resummed and first-order results differ appreciably only for values of $n_s$ outside the favored regions. Finally, we comment on the origin of higher-curvature operators in UV-complete theories, such as renormalizable quantum gravity, where the predictions of the Starobinsky model are stable.
papers.summary: The paper investigates higher-curvature corrections to Starobinsky inflation, showing that naive perturbative expansions in the couplings lead to singularities in the slow-roll parameter. By resumming series in the ratio α/γ, the authors obtain a regular improved slow-roll expansion that reproduces the Starobinsky predictions and matches observational data.

papers.title: Rotational instability and quadrupolar order in BFSS matrix theory
papers.abstract: We study the effect of angular momentum on thermal states of the BFSS matrix theory in its gravitational and high-temperature classical regimes. We focus on ensembles with only one non-zero angular momentum. On the gravity side, the rotating ensemble is described by the singly-spinning D$0$ black hole. Beyond a critical rotation, we find that this solution becomes unstable to a non-axisymmetric quadrupolar perturbation. Following this mode non-linearly, we find a new branch of non-axisymmetric rotating black holes that is thermodynamically favoured over the axisymmetric branch in both the microcanonical and canonical ensembles. On the other hand, in the classical matrix limit, we find no evidence for such collective quadrupolar order over the matrix sizes and angular momenta studied. Instead, rotation accelerates the separation of a single D$0$-brane from the clump of branes initially prepared. The separated brane carries a large fraction of the angular momentum by orbiting the rest of the clump at a large in-plane radius. Both the angular momentum share and the orbital radius relative to the clump size increase with the matrix size. These results distinguish a collective quadrupolar deformation in the gravity limit from angular-momentum transfer to a single brane in the classical matrix limit.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes rotating thermal states of BFSS matrix theory, showing that in the gravity regime a singly-spinning D0 black hole becomes unstable to a quadrupolar perturbation, leading to a new thermodynamically favored non-axisymmetric branch. In contrast, the classical matrix limit exhibits no collective quadrupolar order; instead rotation drives a single D0-brane to separate and carry most of the angular momentum.

papers.title: Scale separation and partial supersymmetry breaking
papers.authors: Niccol\`o Cribiori, Fotis Farakos, Alexandros Zarafonitis
papers.abstract: We propose new candidate string theory vacua in which partial supersymmetry breaking occurs within the lower-dimensional effective theory in anti-de Sitter space, parametrically below the Kaluza--Klein scale. These vacua solve the equations of motion of massless type IIA supergravity in the smeared approximation and exhibit parametric scale separation, at both weak and strong string coupling. They are reproduced as $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric phases of a three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ gauged supergravity. Should these vacua be solutions of string theory, they would provide explicit setups in which partial supersymmetry breaking can be studied at energies parametrically below the compactification scale. In addition, we further comment on our previously proposed solution with scale separation and extended supersymmetry.
papers.summary: The authors construct new type IIA AdS vacua exhibiting parametric scale separation and partial supersymmetry breaking, solved in the smeared approximation and reproduced by a three‑dimensional μ=2 gauged supergravity. These solutions offer a controlled setting to study supersymmetry breaking below the Kaluza–Klein scale, potentially informing holographic duals of non‑maximally supersymmetric CFTs.

papers.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cveti\v{c}-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-St\"ackel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.
papers.summary: This paper presents the most general non‑extremal rotating charged AdS$_4$ black hole in $mathcal{N}=2$ $U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity, with seven independent parameters and a Killing–Stäckel tensor ensuring separability of field equations. It offers a clean, singularity‑free background for studying AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ holography, thermodynamics, and BPS microstate counting.

papers.title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
papers.authors: Christoph Adam, Andr\'es R. Anad\'on, Carlos Naya, Thomas Winyard
papers.abstract: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.
papers.summary: This study presents static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field for baryon numbers up to six, revealing how the field induces isospin‑breaking deformations and novel toroidal chain geometries. The authors employ a GPU‑accelerated arrested Newton flow algorithm to find energy minimizers, showing that gauged skyrmions are more tightly bound and exhibit negative baryon density regions at weak fields.

papers.title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
papers.abstract: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/\omega$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.
papers.summary: This paper shows that the leading exponential rate in high-frequency holographic thermal two-point functions is universal, independent of operator dimension and spin, and is governed by a WKB spectral curve that encodes the black hole singularity. It further derives connection matrices via exact‑WKB, revealing how the singularity influences time‑domain signatures, quasinormal modes, and OPE coefficients in the dual field theory.

papers.title: Giant Graviton Correlators: From Non-maximal to Dual, Bootstrap and Hidden Symmetry
papers.authors: Qi Chen, Zhongjie Huang, Yunfeng Jiang, Xinan Zhou
papers.abstract: We compute four-point functions of two light $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS operators and two heavy giant graviton operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills theory at large $N$ and infinite 't Hooft coupling. Using bootstrap techniques, we determine the correlators for arbitrary light-operator dimensions and arbitrary allowed sizes of non-maximal sphere and dual giant gravitons. We show that these correlators exhibit a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing them to be organized into compact generating functions. Remarkably, the generating functions for both types of giant gravitons can be obtained from the maximal giant case through $SO(2,10)$ rotations in the embedding space.
papers.summary: This work computes four-point correlators of two light 1/2-BPS and two heavy giant graviton operators in N=4 SYM at large N and strong coupling, using bootstrap to obtain results for arbitrary light dimensions and giant sizes. The correlators reveal a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing them to be expressed via generating functions related by SO(2,10) rotations to the maximal giant case.

papers.title: Boundary dualities of symplectic Chern-Simons theories and minimal models
papers.abstract: We propose that a Neumann-type boundary condition of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $USp(2n)$ Chern-Simons theory at the level $-(n+\frac32)$ with a fundamental chiral multiplet is dual to a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of an Abelian rank-$0$ theory. In a topological twist we propose that it supports the affine vertex operator algebra (VOA) $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$. With the corresponding specialization of the fugacities, the line defect half-indices of the antisymmetric Wilson lines give, up to monomials, the supercharacters of all its modules, which coincide up to signs with the characters of the Virasoro minimal model $M(2,2n+3)$. We extend the duality to the level $-(n+\ell+\frac12)$ and propose that the boundary VOA is $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2\ell))$. Together with the Giveon-Kutasov type duality and the mirror symmetry, the proposed dualities form a web of dualities of the boundary conditions and the line operators. For other gauge groups with real matter we propose that the boundary VOA in the holomorphic twist is the commutant of the gauge currents in free real fermions, which is the Ising model for $Spin(7)$ with the spinor and the $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal minimal model $SM(3,5)$ for $G_2$ with $\mathbf7$.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a duality between a Neumann-type boundary condition of a 3d N=2 USp(2n) Chern–Simons theory at level −(n+3/2) with a fundamental chiral multiplet and a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of a rank‑0 Abelian theory, whose topological twist supports the affine VOA L_n(osp(1|2)). The authors identify the line‑defect half‑indices with supercharacters of this VOA, matching the characters of the Virasoro minimal model M(2,2n+3), and extend the construction to higher rank and other gauge groups, linking boundary VOAs to commutants in free fermion theories.

papers.title: Bions and infrared renormalons in K\"ahler sigma models with $U(1)$ isotropy
papers.abstract: We study semiclassical bion contributions to the vacuum energy of K\"ahler sigma models with two-dimensional target spaces on $\mathbb{R} \times S^1$ with twisted boundary conditions. This is first illustrated in the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model, where explicit real and complex bion solutions are constructed in a manner analogous to that used in its quantum-mechanical reduction [1]. Evaluating the bosonic and fermionic fluctuations at one loop, we obtain the effective action with both the coupling constant and the elongation parameter properly renormalized. Integration over the bion quasi-moduli space using Lefschetz thimbles then gives the leading nonperturbative contribution, which the real and complex bion contributions cancel at the supersymmetric point, while the first imaginary ambiguity appears when deviating from the supersymmetric point. Requiring its cancellation against the perturbative ambiguity allows us to infer the corresponding infrared-renormalon pole. This is an explicit example generalizing the resurgent structure of the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model in [2] from one coupling to two renormalized parameters. The calculation further extends to K\"ahler targets of one complex dimension with a $U(1)$ symmetry. At leading dilute one-loop order, the target dependence enters through the moment-map difference and the metric normalizations at the two fixed points. The ambiguity structure and infrared scaling of the bion weight are common to these targets, while the inferred pole position depends on the target metric.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes semiclassical bion solutions in two-dimensional Kähler sigma models on a circle, computing their one-loop fluctuations and Lefschetz thimble integration to extract nonperturbative contributions and infer infrared renormalon poles. The results generalize known resurgent structures from the CP^1 model to a broader class of U(1)-symmetric Kähler targets, highlighting how target geometry influences the renormalon pole position.

papers.title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlev\'e II
papers.authors: Sibasish Banerjee, Babak Haghighat, Jie Sun
papers.abstract: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlev\'e II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlev\'e II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.
papers.summary: This paper develops an irregular KZ–BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlevé II using rank‑three Wakimoto–Whittaker modules, leading to a joint affine system whose Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction produces scalar BPZ equations and matrix‑integral solutions for a single insertion. It further establishes a quantum Langlands duality that exchanges the insertion with the dual Whittaker zero, linking the classical Painlevé II Lax pair to an irregular Gaudin oper in the Nekrasov–Shatashvili limit.

papers.title: Geometry of Gauge-invariant Quantum Fields
papers.abstract: Gauge-invariant representatives of massless gauge fields generally involve inverse differential operators. We trace this non-locality to the homotopy contracting the free gauge complex and replace it, at field level, by a local map using an independent scalar and a differential constraint. We discuss the BRST completion needed to preserve the physical content and the relation to the St\"uckelberg theory. We finally comment on the extension of this approach to non-Abelian gauge groups via the extension to interactions through $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.
papers.summary: The paper develops a local representation of gauge‑invariant massless gauge fields by replacing the usual nonlocal inverse differential operators with a local map that introduces an auxiliary scalar field and a differential constraint, while preserving BRST invariance. It further outlines how this construction can be extended to non‑Abelian gauge theories via L∞ homotopy transfer, providing a systematic framework for handling interactions.

papers.title: Gravitational Particle Production and Locality of the Wavefunction-Squared
papers.abstract: We show that no particle production due to the background geometry implies the locality of the wavefunction-squared for free heavy masses on expanding cosmologies. On global de Sitter of odd dimensions these two stem from the same identity, whereas in the Poincare patch neither occur under any condition. These two phenomena both depend on the behaviour of the out modes at far future and we show that they almost always come together for systems with an out mode that has a phase with separated time and momentum dependency at far future. This will be true for most expanding cosmologies. We comment on how the discussion can be connected to Green's functions and on some previous results in the literature that are seemingly contrary to our conclusions.
papers.summary: The authors prove that the absence of particle production in expanding spacetimes forces the wavefunction‑squared of free heavy fields to be local, with a special identity in odd‑dimensional de Sitter and no such effect in the Poincaré patch. They link this locality to the asymptotic phase structure of out‑modes, discuss its relation to Green’s functions, and reconcile it with earlier contradictory results.

papers.title: Tunneling from an oscillating state in quantum field theory
papers.authors: Oliver Janssen, Matthew Kleban, Mehrdad Mirbabayi, Cameron Norton
papers.abstract: How does a scalar field oscillating about a metastable minimum decay? For a coherent state with $\langle q(t) \rangle = a \cos mt$ we find two results. When $mR \ll 1$, with $m$ the mass and $R$ the bubble radius, the decay at time $t$ is a Coleman bubble in the frozen potential $U_t(\eta) = U(\langle q \rangle +\eta)-U(\langle q \rangle)-U'(\langle q \rangle)\eta$, for any amplitude. At small amplitude but any $mR$, $B(t)=B_0 - a \mathcal{M} \cos mt+O(a^2)$, with $\mathcal{M}$ set by the tail of the vacuum bounce; for a thin wall $\mathcal{M} \propto e^{mR}$, so exponentially small oscillations change the rate significantly. Both results follow from a Euclidean source construction. The same method computes the tunneling rate of a field slowly rolling in one direction and metastable in another.
papers.summary: The paper studies decay of a scalar field oscillating about a metastable minimum, deriving the tunneling rate via a Euclidean source method. It shows that for small oscillation amplitude the decay exponent oscillates with the field, while in the long-wavelength limit the process reduces to a Coleman bubble in a frozen potential.

papers.title: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
papers.abstract: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordstr\"om Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a Landau theory for a continuous phase transition of black branes, using the interior geometry of the Reissner–Nordström black hole and the emergence of a Kasner singularity in the scalarized phase. By relating a conserved radial charge to the grand potential and employing the Iyer–Wald first law, the authors derive critical scaling laws that agree with full numerical solutions.

papers.title: Generalizations of Courant brackets in the T-dual description of a weakly curved string background
papers.abstract: When T-duality is realized as a canonical transformation, the standard Courant bracket is T-dual invariant, while the $B$- and $\theta$-twisted Courant brackets are exchanged. We determine how these relations are modified for a closed bosonic string moving in a weakly curved background with a constant metric and a Kalb-Ramond field with linear coordinate dependence. We work to first order in its constant field strength. The T-dual background fields depend on a line integral of auxiliary worldsheet gauge fields, making the dual description nonlocal. We construct generalized charges whose parameters depend on this line integral and calculate their Poisson bracket algebra using the T-duality transformation laws and the canonical brackets of the initial theory. The resulting algebra yields a weakly curved generalization of the Courant bracket and its associated Courant algebroid. We establish an explicit isomorphism with the standard Courant algebroid by transporting the bracket, pairing, and anchor. Applying $B$- and $\theta$-shifts to the dual currents, we obtain weakly curved generalizations of the respective twisted Courant brackets. We show that these brackets provide the T-dual realizations of the initial $\theta$- and $B$-twisted Courant brackets, respectively, and identify the corresponding Courant algebroid isomorphisms.
papers.summary: The authors extend the Courant bracket to weakly curved string backgrounds by incorporating a linear Kalb-Ramond field and derive its T-dual counterpart via canonical transformations. They show that the resulting algebra reproduces a weakly curved generalization of the Courant algebroid and establish isomorphisms with the standard twisted brackets.

papers.title: Yang-Lee edge singularity at $\mathcal{O}(\partial^4)$ from the functional renormalization group: revised analysis
papers.authors: Konrad Kockler, Jan M. Pawlowski, Vladimir V. Skokov
papers.abstract: We determine the critical exponents of the Yang-Lee edge singularity as continuous functions of dimension using the functional renormalization group, retaining all operators at second and fourth order in the derivative expansion. At fourth order, we obtain $\eta=-0.153(7)$, $-0.352(9)$ and $-0.575(9)$ in $d=5$, $4$ and $3$, respectively, in agreement with the six-loop $\epsilon$ expansion. In three dimensions, these results give $\sigma=0.076$ and $\nu_c=0.359$. We locate the zero of the edge exponent at $d_\sigma=2.65(1)$, also consistent with the six-loop estimate. Continuing the fixed point through $d_\sigma$, we obtain $\eta=-0.795(21)$ and $\omega=1.90(6)$ in $d=2$, compared with the exact values $-4/5$ and $2$.   For the complex Yang-Lee fixed point, convergence of the field expansion depends crucially on its reference point. Expansions about $\phi=0$ fail to converge with the smooth regulator used here, whereas expansions about the running imaginary field value at which the mass vanishes converge down to $d=1.3$. This representation preserves the exact relation between the thermal eigenvalue and the field dimension, and hence the hyperscaling identity $\theta_h+\theta_t=d$, at every field-truncation order. We trace the large violations reported in earlier works to the omission of the expansion-point motion when linearizing the flow, rather than to the truncation itself.
papers.summary: This study refines the determination of critical exponents for the Yang-Lee edge singularity across dimensions using a fourth-order derivative expansion within the functional renormalization group, achieving agreement with high-loop epsilon expansions. It also elucidates convergence issues in complex fixed-point expansions and tracks the fixed point through the critical dimension, offering precise values for exponents in two, three, and four dimensions.

papers.title: Reducing Massive Scattering Amplitudes to Normal Form
papers.abstract: Local amplitude reduction is a crucial tool in effective field theory (EFT) calculations. While polynomial normal forms reproduce the massless y-basis, massive amplitudes require reduction rules that preserve little-group tensor contractions. We generalize Gr\"obner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities, determining leading monomials in their contraction contexts and generating the higher-degree rules induced by mass determinants. Using three-, four-, and five-point replacement catalogs, we demonstrate symbolic-mass amplitude reductions and reproduce the independent three- and four-vector operator bases, providing traceable normal-form reductions for local EFT matching and syzygy analysis.
papers.summary: This work develops a systematic Gr"obner-basis framework for reducing massive scattering amplitudes to a covariant normal form, preserving little‑group tensor structures. It demonstrates explicit three‑, four‑ and five‑point reduction tables and reproduces the independent operator bases needed for EFT matching and syzygy analysis.

papers.title: Multiloop Unitarity from Airy Zeros
papers.abstract: Hidden zeros are non-trivial cancellations that make amplitudes or integrands vanish on specific kinematic loci away from propagator poles. They have been shown to uniquely determine tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands in $\Tr(\phi^3)$ theory, without assuming factorization. Here we extend both the zeros and the uniqueness results to two, three and four loops at arbitrary multiplicity. We show that two types of zeros naturally enter the all-loop problem. First, tree-level zeros extend to all loop orders and fix relative weights within families of subgraphs attached to vacuum ``loop cores.'' We then show that Kontsevich's matrix Airy function can be used to generate a rich structure of loop level zeros that fix the relative weights of the loop cores themselves. The relative factorization and cut data required by unitarity therefore follow from the combination of tree and Airy loop zeros. These results bring within reach the emergence of unitarity to all orders in perturbation theory.
papers.summary: This work extends the concept of hidden zeros—specific kinematic loci where amplitudes vanish—to multiloop orders in scalar φ^3 theory, showing that tree-level and Airy-function-generated zeros uniquely fix loop integrands without invoking factorization. The authors demonstrate that these zeros determine the relative weights of subgraphs and loop cores, thereby recovering unitarity at all perturbative orders.

papers.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
papers.abstract: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using L\"uscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI. Finally, we identify metastable resonances in the spectrum.
papers.summary: This paper numerically solves the ground state of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model, matching bootstrap results and confirming the v^4/r^7 interaction via Lüscher's method. It also discovers positive-energy bound states and metastable resonances, extending the non-perturbative scattering analysis to four-point amplitudes.

papers.title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(\delta t)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $\kappa(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.
papers.summary: This paper develops a constrained mixed variational framework for incremental irreversible thermodynamics, combining penalty terms, Fenchel–Young defects, and multipliers to enforce constitutive relations. It proves algebraic reconstruction of contact fields, establishes energy-drift bounds, and presents a DG0–RT0 discretization that preserves discrete energy.

papers.title: Quantum simulation of real-time bosonic dynamics with binary and unary position encodings on superconducting and trapped-ion processors
papers.authors: Masanori Hanada, Jiwoo Seo, Seok-Kyun Son, Junggi Yoon
papers.abstract: Simulating a bosonic degree of freedom on qubit hardware requires discretizing its position space, and the qubit encoding of the resulting lattice determines the circuits that realize its real-time dynamics. We compare binary and unary encodings of a position lattice on superconducting (IBM) and trapped-ion (IonQ) processors. Binary encoding applies the kinetic term through the quantum Fourier transform; unary encoding uses one qubit per site, single-qubit rotations for the potential and excitation-conserving exchange gates for the kinetic term. For a single degree of freedom the unary dynamics is a free-fermion problem, and its product formula compresses exactly into a nearest-neighbor circuit of fixed size. With about two hundred two-qubit gates, these circuits resolve tunneling in a symmetric double well on both processors, with the right-well probability falling from 0.97 to 0.06 on IBM and from 0.96 to 0.12 on IonQ, whereas binary product-formula circuits with several thousand two-qubit gates do not reproduce the transfer. Noiseless emulation indicates that this contrast reflects the compilation as well as the encoding: without the fixed-size optimization, a unary product formula that captures the transfer also requires several thousand two-qubit gates. Post-selection on the single-excitation subspace removes leakage, and because every energy eigenstate of the symmetric grid populates both wells equally, the measured population reversal bounds the coherence between energy eigenstates from below. Coupled-oscillator benchmarks, where inter-register interactions prevent this exact compression, show that the preferred encoding depends on the grid size and the evolution time.
papers.summary: The authors benchmark binary and unary position encodings for simulating a single bosonic degree of freedom on superconducting and trapped‑ion qubit hardware, showing that the unary encoding—despite its larger Hilbert space—compresses into a fixed‑size nearest‑neighbor circuit that accurately reproduces tunneling in a double‑well potential with only ~200 two‑qubit gates. In contrast, binary product‑formula circuits require several thousand two‑qubit gates and fail to capture the transfer, highlighting the critical role of encoding and compilation for near‑term quantum simulations of bosonic dynamics.

papers.title: Planckian Charge Equilibration in Fast Scramblers
papers.abstract: The Planckian time, $\tau_{\rm Pl}=\hbar/(k_BT)$, is conjectured to set a lower limit on thermal relaxation times in strongly interacting quantum matter. Rigorous bounds limit both how rapidly quantum information can scramble and how soon hydrodynamics can emerge, yet the relation between the scrambling and equilibration rates remains unclear. We address this question by studying the relaxation of a charge imbalance between two subsystems of the complex Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model and its Yukawa generalizations, which exhibit maximal scrambling. In the low-temperature conformal regime, we find through a linear response analysis that the slowest decay of this imbalance occurs at rate $\Gamma=2\pi(2\Delta-d)k_BT/\hbar$, where $\Delta$ is the fermion scaling dimension and $d=0,1$ is the spatial dimension. These results establish Planckian charge equilibration in maximally scrambling systems and show that maximal scrambling alone does not fix its dimensionless prefactor.
papers.summary: This work demonstrates that in maximally scrambling systems such as the complex SYK model, the slowest charge equilibration rate is set by a Planckian timescale with a prefactor determined by the fermion scaling dimension and spatial dimension. The analysis shows that maximal scrambling does not uniquely fix the equilibration prefactor, highlighting a subtle distinction between scrambling and thermal relaxation.

papers.title: Time Direction Entanglement Entropy of Free Fermion Ground States
papers.authors: Xinyu Sun, Bowei Liu, Joshua Yi, Biao Lian
papers.abstract: While the entanglement entropy of a spatial subregion has been extensively studied, a properly defined entanglement entropy of quantum states in a time direction interval remains underexplored. We investigate the scaling behaviors of the recently defined time direction entanglement entropy (TDEE) for free fermion quantum states, which is computed from the reduced density matrix of a sub-Hilbert space that minimally supports all the time-evolved operators in the time direction interval. Based on the Fisher--Hartwig conjecture for Toeplitz matrices, we develop an analytical framework for understanding the TDEE in a time interval with discrete time step $\tau$. For disorderless one-dimensional (1D) systems (gapless fermions or band insulators), in different regimes of gap, bandwidth and $\tau$, we find the TDEE can exhibit area law (for nonzero gap), logarithmic law or volume law in the length of time. For 1D Anderson insulators, we numerically find the TDEE shows a Page-curve like behavior, growing at short time, and decaying in power-law at long time exceeding the crossover time determined by localization. In the continuum time limit $\tau\rightarrow 0$, the TDEE of disorderless gapless fermions, band insulators and Anderson insulators exhibit logarithmic law, area law and sub-area law, respectively. We also show that the sub-Hilbert space of a time-direction interval stabilizes in the $\tau\rightarrow 0$ limit, which is understandable as a subspace of the Hilbert space of the Lieb-Robinson causal diamond.
papers.summary: This work defines a time-direction entanglement entropy (TDEE) for free fermion ground states by tracing over a sub-Hilbert space that supports all time-evolved operators within a discrete time interval. Using the Fisher–Hartwig conjecture for Toeplitz matrices, the authors analytically characterize scaling regimes (area, logarithmic, volume laws) and numerically observe Page‑curve‑like behavior in Anderson insulators, with a continuum limit yielding logarithmic, area, and sub‑area laws for gapless, gapped, and localized systems, respectively.

papers.title: Comment to: "Rewording Theoretical Predictions at Colliders with Vacuum Amplitudes"
papers.abstract: This comment highlights flaws in two central results presented by Ram\'irez-Uribe et al. in the titular letter, Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 211901 (2024) [arXiv:2404.05491]. Firstly, the authors incorrectly claim that integrands of differential scattering cross-sections are obtained as single "residues" of vacuum amplitudes, although a sharp distinction of initial and final states requires to consider two iterated discontinuities. Secondly, they wrongly state that non-pinched thresholds always locally match in such a differential representation.
papers.summary: This comment points out two technical errors in a recent PRL on vacuum amplitudes: (1) the claim that differential cross‑section integrands are single residues is incorrect, as one must use two iterated discontinuities to separate initial and final states; (2) the assertion that non‑pinched thresholds always match locally in such a representation is false. The critique clarifies the proper analytic structure needed for scattering amplitude calculations.

papers.title: Off-shell continuation from on-shell recursion
papers.authors: Wenqi Ke, Zhen Liu, Ishmam Mahbub
papers.abstract: Starting from on-shell factorization and the polarization sum of an internal massive vector, we provide an off-shell continuation of the transverse and longitudinal contributions defined at arbitrary virtuality. The construction relies on on-shell constructibility and the three-point off-shell current constraint $p \cdot J = O(m)$. For amplitudes with external longitudinal vectors, we develop a method that isolates the mass-singular contributions associated with the longitudinal polarization, namely terms with power-law singularities in the massless limit. In the examples studied, these terms appear as contact contributions in individual factorization channels, and we identify the conditions under which they cancel. We give an independent understanding, based on massive on-shell amplitudes, of the polarization decomposition and diagram-by-diagram high-energy power counting underlying the Feynman-Diagram gauge and related five-component formulations. We further clarify how higher-point current constraints can emerge from on-shell constructibility and the cancellation of mass singularities. We illustrate the mechanism with explicit four-point examples and discuss the constraints imposed by a smooth massless limit. The work provides a systematic bottom-up method for building massive amplitudes free of mass-singular terms and opens a route toward a broader amplitude-based understanding of field decompositions, connecting massive and massless descriptions and on-shell states with off-shell descriptions.
papers.summary: The paper develops an off‑shell continuation of on‑shell recursion for massive vector amplitudes, providing a systematic way to isolate and cancel mass‑singular terms in longitudinal polarizations. It clarifies the role of higher‑point current constraints and offers a bottom‑up construction of massive amplitudes free of singularities, with potential applications to gauge theory and high‑energy power counting.

papers.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
papers.authors: Aliv Sahoo, Fatima Abbasi, Jake McNaughton, Niayesh Afshordi
papers.abstract: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-\Gamma H^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $\Gamma={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $\sigma\equiv\Gamma/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $\sigma$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2\sigma/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(\sigma m_\nu^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $\Gamma=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$\Gamma$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $\Gamma\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($\sigma\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a minimal modification to the Raychaudhuri equation inspired by fast‑scrambling arguments, yielding a slowly evolving vacuum described by a Lambert‑W solution that behaves like dark energy with a small deviation from w=−1 and a history‑dependent component. It finds that the parameter Γ≈−3 fits BBN, CMB, BAO and SN data, reproduces w0waCDM‑like evolution, and motivates detailed structure‑formation analyses.

papers.title: Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality
papers.abstract: We study mirror map derivatives as a means of relating the genus zero Gromov-Witten theories of an anticanonical Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a smooth, almost minimal Fano variety and the local Calabi-Yau formed from the total space of the Fano's canonical bundle with the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano. A precise relationship between reciprocal mirror map derivatives is obtained from the non-equivariant limit of quantum Serre duality for the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano as formulated by Iritani, Mann, & Mignon. This allows us to express the generating series of 3-point euler-twisted invariants as the derivative of the local mirror map with respect to the closed one. In low dimensions, this series is shown to be a modular form of Eisenstein type which has arisen before in this area. We prove integrality of the twisted invariants from this identification. The regularized small quantum $D$-module of the Fano is reducible, and we show it is equivalent to an inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation governed by this generating series. The reciprocal mirror map derivative is then shown to be a generating function of local 3-point invariants, which recovers some known results for local Calabi-Yau threefolds and proves a conjecture of the second named author and A. Malmendier in previous work on local fourfolds. Explicit calculations for $\mathbb{P}^2,\mathbb{P}^3$ and $\mathbb{P}^4$ illustrate these relationships, which includes the vanishing of positive-degree ordinary genus-zero invariants for anticanonical elliptic curves and K3 surfaces, the recovery of the quintic threefold's instanton numbers, and finally some formulas for genus-zero invariants of local projective spaces.
papers.summary: This work establishes a precise link between derivatives of the mirror map for anticanonical Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces and Euler‑twisted Gromov–Witten invariants of the ambient Fano, using quantum Serre duality to express local 3‑point invariants as modular forms. It further shows integrality of these invariants, derives Picard–Fuchs equations, and verifies conjectures for local Calabi–Yau threefolds and fourfolds, with explicit examples in projective spaces.

papers.title: The KLN theorem meets collinear factorisation: Local Unitarity for hadronic cross-sections
papers.abstract: We present an initial-state implementation of the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg (KLN) theorem that is compatible with collinear factorisation. In this formulation, hadronic cross-sections are expressed as convolutions of parton distribution functions with partonic cross-sections obtained by summing over the number of incoming partons. By virtue of the KLN theorem, the partonic cross-sections are infrared finite by construction, without relying on dimensional regularisation as an infrared regulator. The Local Unitarity formalism provides a local realisation of this infrared finiteness, allowing partonic cross-sections to be evaluated directly in four dimensions by Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the framework at next-to-leading order and leading power. Using Local Unitarity, we compute the Drell-Yan and $t\bar{t}$ production cross-sections numerically; using Reverse Unitarity, we obtain the deep inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan cross-sections analytically. In all cases, a universal scheme conversion relates our results to those obtained in the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ parton model.
papers.summary: This work introduces an initial‑state implementation of the KLN theorem that preserves collinear factorisation, enabling infrared‑finite partonic cross‑sections to be computed directly in four dimensions via Local Unitarity. The authors validate the method at NLO for Drell‑Yan, top‑pair production, and DIS, showing agreement with standard MSbar results.

papers.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
papers.authors: Robin Croft, Gerardo Garc\'ia-Moreno, Paolo Pani
papers.abstract: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.
papers.summary: This study tests the hoop conjecture in rotating, axisymmetric dust configurations, finding that the conjecture remains valid when rotational energy is included in the quasilocal mass, but fails when using ADM mass or irreducible mass for high spin. The work also examines horizonless configurations and their implications for weak cosmic censorship and horizonless compact objects.

papers.title: Thermal $CP$ dynamics in a four-fermion model: mean-field and functional renormalization group analyses
papers.authors: Arthur F. Vieira, Rudnei O. Ramos
papers.abstract: We investigate a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed scalar-pseudoscalar interactions at finite temperature and vanishing chemical potential. Our analysis combines the mean-field approximation, which determines the equilibrium condensates, with the functional renormalization group (FRG), which describes the scale dependence of the interactions and the fermion mass phase. Within the mean-field approach, we find that, in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking sources, the dominant interaction determines the direction of condensation. In particular, a pseudoscalar condensate spontaneously breaks the ordinary $P/CP$ symmetry and disappears through a continuous thermal phase transition. For regular high-temperature FRG trajectories, the dimensionless mixed coupling tends to zero in the infrared, while its dimensionful counterpart remains finite. Increasing temperature also suppresses the scale evolution of the fermion mass phase. Together, these results clarify the distinct roles of thermal fluctuations in suppressing spontaneous symmetry breaking and fermionic instabilities, without necessarily eliminating explicit symmetry breaking effects.
papers.summary: This paper studies a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed interactions at finite temperature using mean-field and functional renormalization group methods. It finds that a pseudoscalar condensate breaks CP symmetry and disappears via a continuous thermal phase transition, while the mixed coupling flows to zero in the infrared, illustrating how thermal fluctuations suppress spontaneous symmetry breaking.

papers.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
papers.abstract: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.
papers.summary: The paper develops a geometric framework for the q‑deformed differential equation/ODE/IM correspondence in ADE Lie algebras, interpreting shifted monodromy as twisted (G,q)-opers and constructing a universal (G,q)-Wronskian that encodes Q‑functions obeying QQ‑relations. It connects these structures to quantum‑affine q‑characters and verifies the analytic conditions for Feigin–Frenkel–Hernandez affine opers, thereby linking affine opers to twisted (G,q)-opers in a way that resonates with the quantum Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.
papers.summary: This paper develops a classical LSZ-like reduction for scalar-induced gravitational waves, identifying the free radiation as the out-state of tensor perturbations in a perfect fluid with constant equation of state. It shows that the out-state is gauge invariant across intrinsic gauges and justifies using the late-time Newtonian kernel for the energy spectrum of the free radiation.

papers.title: Elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals for orthogonal groups and Seiberg duality on the lens space
papers.abstract: We derive new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with the orthogonal groups $\mathrm{SO}(N)$. The sum/integrals are written in terms of the lens elliptic gamma function, which depends on an integer $r\geq 1$ in addition to the usual complex variables, and they reduce to the elliptic hypergeometric integrals of Spiridonov and Vartanov for $r=1$. The derivation uses the $BC_n\leftrightarrow BC_{\tilde n}$ transformation formula proven in our previous paper, together with a duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function proven here. The duplication formula takes a different form depending on whether $r$ is even or odd. Physically, the new transformations show that the supersymmetric lens indices on $S^1\times S^3/\mathbb{Z}_r$ of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ and $\mathrm{SO}(N_f-N+4)$ gauge theories related by Seiberg duality are equal for odd $r$. For even $r$, where the lens index depends on the global form of the gauge group, they show the equality of the contributions from flat connections whose holonomies lie in a common maximal torus. The $BC_n$ formula itself gives the corresponding statement for the symplectic groups.
papers.summary: The paper derives new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with orthogonal groups, using a duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function and a BC_n↔BC_{	ilde n} transformation. These results confirm that supersymmetric lens indices for Seiberg-dual SO(N) gauge theories agree for odd r, and relate contributions from flat connections for even r, extending analogous statements to symplectic groups.

papers.title: Three Dimensional Structure of Pion with One Dynamical Gluon in the Light-Cone Quark Model
papers.authors: Satyajit Puhan, Shubham Sharma, Narinder Kumar
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional structure of the pion beyond the leading Fock state by including a dynamical gluon, $|\pi\rangle=|q\bar q\rangle+|q\bar q g\rangle$. Within the light-cone quark model, we calculate the pion GPDs, TMDs, and PDFs from light-front wave function overlaps, using a modified Brodsky--Huang--Lepage wave function with the Melosh--Wigner rotation for the valence sector and the light-front quark--gluon vertex for the $q\bar q g$ sector. The quark-number and momentum sum rules are satisfied without additional constraints. We further obtain the electromagnetic form factor and the mass decomposition. After NLO evolution, we compare the PDFs with pion-induced Drell--Yan, $J/\psi$, $\Upsilon$, and HERA leading-neutron $F_2^\pi$ data. The $q\bar q g$ sector contributes little to Drell--Yan but becomes important for gluon-sensitive observables such as $J/\psi$ production and the pion structure function at small $x$.
papers.summary: This work extends the light‑cone quark model of the pion to include a dynamical gluon component, enabling the calculation of GPDs, TMDs, PDFs, and the electromagnetic form factor from wave‑function overlaps. After NLO evolution the resulting PDFs agree with Drell–Yan and small‑x data, while the gluon sector mainly affects gluon‑sensitive observables such as J/ψ production.

papers.title: Assessing the expressive power of a gauge-invariant PEPS ansatz across a topological phase transition
papers.abstract: We investigate the expressive power of the gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair state (GGFPEPS) ansatz, which is a manifestly gauge-invariant tensor network ansatz for $(2+1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theories. In the GGFPEPS ansatz, the gauge field on each link is represented by coupling its configuration to the fermion number of virtual fermions placed at both ends of the link. This ansatz has been studied by variational Monte Carlo (VMC) methods in previous work~\cite{Emonts:2022yom}. However, the statistical error of VMC makes a precise determination of the variational parameters difficult, so that the expressive power of the ansatz could not be examined accurately. In this work, we reformulate the computation as a Grassmann tensor network (TN), in which the whole network is contracted deterministically, and introduce the higher-order tensor renormalization group (HOTRG), which allows us to perform calculations in large volumes up to $L=34$. We also evaluate the infinite volume system using the corner transfer matrix renormalization group (CTMRG). We find that the ansatz with only eight complex variational parameters accurately describes the pure $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory including the region of the topological phase transition, not only in the energy but also in the topological entanglement entropy. The critical coupling obtained from the peaks of their susceptibilities agrees quantitatively with the one predicted by continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo simulations~\cite{wu2012phase}. Furthermore, near the transition point, we show that the ansatz represents a state outside the plaquette product family, which is a one-parameter family of states assumed in the construction of the ansatz as a simple interpolation between the strong and weak coupling limits.
papers.summary: This work demonstrates that a gauge‑invariant Gaussian fermionic PEPS ansatz with only eight variational parameters can accurately capture the physics of the 2+1D Z₂ lattice gauge theory across its topological phase transition, including energy and topological entanglement entropy, by employing deterministic Grassmann tensor‑network contractions and HOTRG/CTMRG techniques. The authors confirm the critical coupling via susceptibility peaks, matching continuous‑time quantum Monte Carlo results, and show the ansatz extends beyond the simple plaquette product family near criticality.

papers.title: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We present a lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories on the boundary of a slab. The formulation is gauge-fixed, so the gauge variables are the physical modes of the boundary field, and Gauss's law holds exactly. The bulk gauge field is determined by the boundary field and an integer label, which is the topological charge that the boundary generates and the bulk stores as a localized instanton. The bulk enters as a dielectric, and both gauge anomaly conditions become the question of whether the boundary satisfies Gauss's law on its own.
